business_model.claim: MSG Entertainment is a live entertainment company that earns its money from a portfolio of venues (The Garden, Infosys Theater, Radio City Music Hall, Beacon Theatre, The Chicago Theatre), its Christmas Spectacular production, and a concert, family show and sports bookings business. It reports as one segment.
quotes: As of June 30, 2026, we managed our business through one reportable segment.
We operate and report financial information in one reportable segment.

business_model.basis: stated in the income statement and the MD&A table
business_model.claim: Revenue comes from three reported lines. In the quarter ended September 30, 2026 these were entertainment offerings of 174,851, food, beverage and merchandise of 35,693, and arena license fees and other leasing of 6,590, for total revenues of 217,134 (all table figures in thousands of dollars).

Most events are licensed to third-party promoters for a fee, so the company earns venue license fees and does not carry the event's economic risk. It also promotes or co-promotes some shows, which exposes it to that risk.
quotes: Although we primarily license our venues to third-party promoters for a fee, we also promote or co-promote shows.

business_model.claim: Suite licenses at The Garden are sold mainly to corporate customers, usually on multi-year terms with annual escalators. The company also sells sponsorship and signage rights, so corporate customers and sponsors are a recurring revenue base alongside ticket buyers and promoters.
quotes: Suite licenses at The Garden are generally sold to corporate customers with the majority being multi-year licenses with annual escalators.

business_model.claim: The Knicks and Rangers are anchor customers under Arena License Agreements that run for 35 years, through 2055. They pay annual license fees to play all home games at The Garden. The company also shares suite, food and beverage, and certain sponsorship revenue with them.
quotes: Under the Arena License Agreements, which each have a term of 35 years running through 2055, the Knicks and the Rangers pay an annual license fee in connection with their respective use of The Garden.

business_model.claim: The revenue sharing with MSG Sports raises costs when the shared revenue rises. MSG Sports receives 67.5% of suite license revenue and 50% of net proceeds from in-venue food and beverage sales at its games. Those payments are booked in direct operating expenses.
quotes: The revenue sharing expense recognized by the Company for MSG Sports’ share of suite license revenue at The Garden is based on a 67.5% allocation to MSG Sports pursuant to the Arena License Agreements.
The Arena License Agreements require the Company to pay 50% of the net proceeds generated from in-venue food and beverage sales to MSG Sports.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited items; the timing outside the September quarter is inferred from the holiday-season description
business_model.claim: The Christmas Spectacular is a major, concentrated and seasonal driver. The 2025 production was 18% of revenue in the latest fiscal year. It had 215 performances in the 2025 holiday season, against 200 the year before. The company plans 231 performances for the 2026 season.
quotes: The financial results of our business are dependent on the Christmas Spectacular production, for which the 2025 production represented 18% of our revenues in Fiscal Year 2026.
The Company had 215 Christmas Spectacular performances during Fiscal Year 2026’s holiday season, as compared to 200 performances during Fiscal Year 2025’s holiday season.

business_model.claim: Concerts were the main driver of the latest quarter's revenue growth. Concert revenue rose $30.1 million on more concerts at The Garden and higher per-concert revenue, partly offset by fewer concerts at the company's theaters. Food and beverage sales at concerts rose $12.5 million, and other live events and sports rose $11.2 million.
quotes: Revenues from concerts increased $30.1 million, reflecting an increase in the number of concerts at The Garden and higher per-concert revenue, partially offset by a decrease in the number of concerts at the Company's theaters.

business_model.basis: stated in the annual MD&A table
business_model.claim: Over the full fiscal year, total revenues rose 13% to 1,060,784 from 942,734 (table in thousands of dollars). quotes: All dollar amounts included in the following MD&A are presented in thousands, except as otherwise noted.

business_model.claim: The main costs are payments to performers, staging, day-of-event costs, advertising, and the cost of owning, leasing and running the venues. In the latest quarter direct operating expenses were 126,755, against 102,370 a year earlier, and selling, general and administrative expenses were 66,862, against 56,585 (table in thousands of dollars).
quotes: Our principal expenses are payments made to performers of our productions, staging costs and day-of-event costs associated with events, and advertising costs.

business_model.claim: Selling, general and administrative expense growth in the latest quarter was mainly employee compensation and related benefits.

business_model.claim: The company owns The Garden, the Infosys Theater and The Chicago Theatre, and leases Radio City Music Hall and the Beacon Theatre. Business is concentrated in New York City, and the lease terms are a fixed cost base.

business_model.claim: A New York City real estate tax exemption on the Madison Square Garden Complex lowers the company's cost. If it were repealed, the teams would owe the property tax and the annual license fee they pay the company would fall on a percentage basis.
quotes: For Fiscal Year 2026, the tax exemption was $45 million.

competitive_position.claim: Revenue depends heavily on one production and one city. The 2025 Christmas Spectacular was 18% of Fiscal Year 2026 revenue, and operations are concentrated in New York City.

The Company primarily operates in New York City and, as a result, is subject to greater degrees of risk than competitors with more operating properties or that operate in more markets.

competitive_position.claim: A change to the New York City real estate tax exemption for the Madison Square Garden Complex is a named threat. The exemption was worth $45 million in Fiscal Year 2026, and repeal would require action by the New York State legislature.
